answer: To resist sybil attacks the agent economy uses a single controlled inlet that accepts only identities continuously forging unique work tokens from exclusive local entropy sources. An attacker seeking an ocean of fake agents must dedicate distinct non-shareable compute to each forge process; shared hardware yields identical timing signatures the inlet rejects, so the attacker must purchase and power separate machines whose energy and capital costs grow linearly with the number of sybils and quickly exceed any gains from the fakes.
